newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Ssangyong rules out sale of company.
newsitem.headline: Ssangyong rules out sale of company.

text.p: Ssangyong Motor Co, a South Korean producer of utility vehicles, said on Friday it would not sell the company despite growing losses.
A Ssangyong spokesman said the company was seeking a joint venture with foreign firms, including three major U.S. carmakers.
"We will never sell our company to anyone," Ssangyong spokesman Cho Min-kyun said, denying persistent talk on the stock market that Ssangyong was negotiating its own sale to

Ssangyong, which is 3.62 percent owned by Mercedes-Benz, a subsidiary of Daimler-Benz AG, said it would seek technical help from the German company to develop an export model aimed at the Asian market, he said.
Ssangyong, which is expected to register a loss of about 130 billion won for calendar 1996, has set a target of posting a profit in two to three years, Cho said.
Ssangyong said earlier it wanted to cut the loss to about 50 billion won in 1997. It has set 1997 sales target at two trillion won, against an estimated 1.38 trillion won in 1996.
The company said it would start marketing luxury sedans in October which were being developed with the assistance of Mercedes-Benz.
"We plan to churn out about 30,000 units per year, of which 50 percent are for export," Cho said of the luxury car.
Cho declined to give details on ventures Ssangyong was seeking but said: "The negotiations are at initial stages."
